task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: How is 'travel better' (portability) defined and measured for movers?
Is n=24 enough to compare two role subtypes?
How reliable is the cut-heavy vs drive-heavy label derived from play-type records?
How to separate portability from team context, teammates and selection into moves?
Do labels regress to the mean or drift across seasons?

historical_evidence.finding: Portability feasibility gate (Structural Influence, Paper 1): the gate passed. The preregistration recorded 296 movers, decoy fraction 1.00 and vacuity rho=0.048; the final output recorded 294 movers and rho=0.007. Gates were G1 >=25 movers, G2 >=80% of movers with >=3 decoys, G3 |rho|<0.90. [prior work] notes that mover count and rho changed between the prereg record and the final output. Validation: no_validation_recorded.
Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap among initiators: mean gap +0.427 PPP. Limited by small samples: only 3 players reach n>=30 in both tiers. Risk recorded: SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.
Descriptive player/team tier tendencies; player samples of 10-178 possessions; no outcome test.
Inferred-label defensive scheme change: label could not separate real change from noise (near-uniform transition matrices). Recorded limitation: label_or_classification_error (RISK:LABEL_ERROR).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring categorical labels from play-by-play-derived records and then testing change or stability in them
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable / label_or_classification_error: the inferred label cannot separate real change from execution differences, and the near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-level comparisons with thin per-cell possession counts
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limitation small_sample: only 3 players reach n>=30 in both tiers, so most cells fall below the sample gate.

evidence_establishes: A portability feasibility gate has been run on movers ([prior work][prior work], status supported). About 294-296 movers exist and the displacement signature is not collinear with play-type profile (rho ~0.007-0.048).
Player-level play-type comparisons in this project have been limited by sample size ([prior work][prior work]).
Labels inferred from play-by-play have previously been vulnerable to label noise ([prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Nothing retrieved tests whether cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.
The retrieved records do not show how 'shaper', 'cut-heavy' or 'drive-heavy' are defined or how reliable those labels are.
The gate result is not a comparison of subtypes. It does not show how many of the 294 movers are shapers, or how many fall in each subtype.
The retrieved records give no outcome measure of 'travel better' and no validation (validation recorded as none).
own_inferences: If n=24 means 24 shaper units split across two subtypes (~12 each), the comparison is badly underpowered except for very large effects.
If the 24 units are not movers, portability cannot be measured directly. Movers (~294) would be the right population, and the shaper subset must be counted first.

Defining the subtype from the same possessions used to measure role strength creates a mechanical link and possible regression to the mean, so labels should be set on pre-move data and outcomes measured post-move.
Cutting is a low-usage, teammate-dependent action, so cut-heavy roles may look portable or non-portable partly through the quality of the passer on the new team (CONFOUNDING).
The mover gate was changed between prereg and final output (mover count and rho differ), so any reuse of it should freeze the version before analysis.
uncertainties: What the 24 units are and how many are movers.
Whether 'shaper' is already operationalised in the project, and how.
How 'travel better' is to be measured: role-signature persistence, influence retention or efficiency retention.
Whether the 2025-26 data, partial at some earlier dates, are now complete (complete from 2026-04-13 and 2026-06-21, so complete as of 2026-08-08).
Retrieval returned only 4 families and none is directly on shapers; I did not search further.

historical_effect.explanation: [prior work] moved me from a possible simple proceed toward proceed_with_changes. [prior work][prior work] shows a mover population large enough to support a mover-level design, which gives a viable route. [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work] warn of thin cells and label noise, so I added a subtype-count gate and pre-move labelling, and made a descriptive-only outcome the fallback.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 split into two subtypes gives roughly 12 per arm, which is not enough to detect a moderate difference in portability.
'Travel better' and the cut-heavy/drive-heavy labels have no recorded operational definition or reliability estimate.

prior_work.summary: The feasibility gate for portability in general passed ([prior work][prior work]). No retrieved record compares cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers, so the question is not answered.

risks.text: The subtype comparison has ~12 units per arm, or an unknown number of movers per arm.
Cuts and drives that start a recorded possession are sparse per player and per team, so signatures built from them are noisy, especially after a move.
Split-half reliability of the subtype label and of the portability metric is unknown.
Labels inferred from play-by-play have been noisy in this project ([prior work][prior work]).
Players selected as extreme cut-heavy or drive-heavy will regress toward the mean on their post-move profile.
Teammates, coach system, usage change and selection into moves are all confounded with the role subtype.
If the subtype and the portability outcome come from the same possessions, the comparison is partly mechanical.
Classifying a player with post-move data leaks the outcome into the label.
Several portability metrics and several thresholds would inflate false positives.
League play style changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26, and the recorded mover count changed between prereg and final output.

design.estimand: Difference between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers in role-signature persistence after changing teams. Persistence is the within-player correlation of the role profile before and after the move, measured against the same persistence for non-moving players over matched windows.
design.unit: Shaper-mover (player who changed team between seasons or mid-season), not the 24 units as stated unless they are confirmed to be movers.
design.sample: Freeze the data version on 2026-08-08, covering 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs. Start from the ~294 movers in [prior work][prior work]. Define shaper, cut-heavy and drive-heavy from pre-move possessions only, with a minimum possession count fixed in advance. Gate: at least 25 shaper-movers per arm with enough pre- and post-move possessions. If the gate fails, report a descriptive result only, with no hypothesis test.
design.power: Compute before analysis from the observed per-arm counts and the split-half reliability of the persistence metric. With ~12 per arm only very large differences are detectable (roughly d > 1.2 at 80% power), so n=24 does not support a confirmatory test. The decision rule requires the minimum detectable effect to be stated in advance.
design.controls: Pre-move usage, minutes, position, age and team quality. Control for new-team passer quality and pace. Handle regression to the mean by using reliability-adjusted or shrunken labels and a continuous cut-minus-drive share as the primary exposure, with the binary split as a sensitivity check. Use the non-mover persistence baseline.
design.falsification: Placebo: randomly reassign subtype labels within shaper-movers, and apply the same analysis to non-movers across consecutive seasons. A difference in non-movers means the effect reflects subtype stability, not portability. A swap-and-reverse check: set the label on post-move data and confirm the sign of any effect changes or vanishes.
design.multiplicity: One pre-specified primary metric (persistence of role profile) and one primary contrast. Any secondary metrics (influence retention, efficiency retention) are labelled exploratory and corrected with Holm.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the primary contrast favours cut-heavy shapers, the 95% interval excludes zero, the placebo and non-mover checks show no comparable effect, and the per-arm gate is met. Rejected if the gate is met and the interval lies within a pre-set equivalence margin around zero. Otherwise inconclusive. Keep the gate thresholds and mover count fixed once preregistered, and log any later change.
design.data_version: NBA per-game files and the Neo4j play-type possession records as of 2026-08-08, with 2025-26 regular season (complete 2026-04-13) and playoffs (complete 2026-06-21). Freeze the extract, hash it and record it with the preregistration.
